decisive_items: developed a dry cough and dyspnea on moderate exertion

High-resolution chest CT showed ground-glass interstitial infiltrates with a centrifugal distribution, predominantly in the upper lobes, and a mosaic pattern of disseminated attenuation without lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion
Pulmonary auscultation revealed scant basal “Velcro”-like crackles
response.rationale: Temporal association with etanercept initiation and interstitial lung disease pattern strongly supports etanercept-induced ILD; R9 is a broader category without the specific drug attribution.

rejected.why: Less specific than R1; lacks drug attribution despite same clinical picture.
No evidence of inflammatory bowel disease; spondyloarthropathy is not IBD-associated ILD.
Idiopathic interstitial pneumonia is excluded by clear drug exposure and underlying inflammatory disease.
GeneXpert and silver stain negative; no fever or classic TB pattern.
No exposure history to antigens; absence of fever and systemic symptoms argues against hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
No lymphadenopathy or typical sarcoid features; negative HLA-B27 and spondyloarthropathy context.
Too generic; does not capture etanercept causality.
Patient has seronegative spondyloarthropathy, not rheumatoid arthritis; no RA features.
